title: Learning-science evidence for presenting real-world knowledge inside a fiction/game world on the endia.de knowledge-platform (learning effects and fact-fiction source monitoring)
question: What does empirical learning-science research establish about whether factual knowledge embedded inside a fictional narrative or game world — as the Endia books and the endia.de knowledge-platform do — is learned, retained, and correctly source-attributed (real vs. fictional) by young-adult readers, and which evidence-based design guardrails (clear fiction/fact signalling, debriefing, retrieval practice, source labels) follow so the platform can preserve the canon-evidence boundary without degrading learning?
why_now: ECO-ARC-0016 assigns endia.de the knowledge-platform role, yet this repository is still an onboarding scaffold with no educational concept or fact/fiction presentation rules specified. The worldbuilding-scientific evidence profile makes the canon/evidence boundary a core requirement, so deciding now — on empirical evidence rather than intuition — how a book-framed platform presents real-world topics determines the site's core design before any content is built. The two queued topics that look adjacent do not answer this: the transmedia/games-in-literature topic covers narrative-game design precedents, and the digital-rights topic covers which content to draw on; neither addresses whether and how knowledge framed by fiction is actually learned and correctly attributed.
real_world_anchor: Peer-reviewed learning-science literature on narrative-embedded learning, the seductive-details effect, multimedia learning, and source monitoring in educational media for young adults
novelty_reason: Orthogonal to prior candidates: RES-20260826-868027AD asks which transmedia/game-in-literature design precedents make the in-book game coherent; RES-20260826-47CC2438 asks which digital-rights discourse and literacy content to draw on. Neither poses the empirical question of whether knowledge delivered inside a fictional frame is learned, retained and correctly attributed as fact vs. canon, nor which fact/fiction signalling guardrails the platform needs. This is therefore not a rephrasing or narrowing of either.
